chunks: He said: and Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated to me, from Dawud al-Sarmi, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me:

Whoever comes to you and says to you that this son of mine has become sick, and he closed his eyes, washed him, placed him in his grave niche, and shook off the dust from his grave with his hand, do not believe him.

key_terms.لَحْدِهِ: his grave niche (a specific type of grave structure)
key_terms.نَضَحَ يَدَهُ: he shook his hand (to remove dust)

ai.seo_question: What sign did Imam al-Sadiq give to distinguish between a real death and a fabricated report of death regarding Imam Musa al-Kadhim?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* provides a critical criterion for identifying the Waqifiya, who claimed Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.) had died and ceased to be the Imam. The Imam (a.s.) explains that the physical acts of washing, closing the eyes, and placing the body in the grave were standard burial rites that could be easily mimicked or fabricated, making them unreliable evidence of actual death. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between superficial appearances and the enduring reality of the Imam’s life and authority during the Minor and Major Gheebah.
